results.name: UAP sighting rate differs on geomagnetic storm days vs calm days
results.description: Compare mean daily sighting count on storm days (Kp ≥ 5) vs calm days. A ratio > 1.0 means more sightings on storm days; < 1.0 could indicate weather-correlated suppression (storms often coincide with cloud cover). Stratified by era to control for secular reporting trends.
results.summary: Mean daily sightings: storm days 4.20 vs calm days 6.01 (ratio: 0.70x). Cohen's d = -0.211. Era breakdown: 1990-2005: 0.91x, 2006-2015: 1.14x, 2016-2026: 0.91x.

results.name: UAP sighting distribution across Kp bands deviates from uniform expectation
results.description: Bin sightings by the max Kp on their date into bands (0-1, 1-2, ..., 8-9) and compare the observed distribution to the expected distribution based on how many days fall in each band.
results.summary: χ²(9) = 8876.8. Sighting distribution across Kp bands significantly deviates from the day-count baseline.

results.name: UAP sightings cluster near recent earthquakes
results.description: For each earthquake M4.0+, count sightings within 150 km and ±7 days. Baseline uses time-shifted control: same spatial pairs but with earthquake dates shifted ±90 days to break any real temporal association while preserving geographic co-location.
results.summary: 6524 real sighting–earthquake pairs (within 150 km, ±7 days). Control (±90-day shift): 6218 pairs. Ratio: 1.05x. 3158 earthquakes had nearby sightings.

results.name: UAP sightings are disproportionately concentrated near nuclear facilities
results.description: Compare the fraction of sightings within 80 km of nuclear facilities to control sets of the same size (140 random sighting locations). Controls for population density and geographic reporting bias.
results.summary: 22.4% of sightings within 80 km of nuclear facilities. Control (20 random sets of 140 sighting locations): 54.0% ± 1.6%. Ratio: 0.42x. z = -19.51.

results.name: UAP sightings spike on days with NASA CNEOS fireball events
results.description: Compare the mean sighting count on fireball days vs non-fireball days within the dataset overlap period.
results.summary: Mean sightings on fireball days: 14.2 vs non-fireball days: 7.6 (ratio: 1.87x). Cohen's d = 0.731.

results.name: UAP sightings are more frequent on weekends (observer bias)
results.description: Test whether Friday–Sunday accounts for a disproportionate share of sightings vs Monday–Thursday. Expected: 3/7 = 42.9%.
results.summary: 45.3% of sightings on Fri–Sun vs expected 42.9%. Overrepresentation: 1.057x. χ²(1) = 493.0.
results.testSource:
const { sightings } = ctx

let weekend = 0
let weekday = 0

for (const s of sightings) {
  const d = new Date(s.occurredAt)
  if (isNaN(d.getTime())) continue
  const dow = d.getUTCDay() // 0=Sun, 6=Sat
  if (dow === 0 || dow === 5 || dow === 6) weekend++
  else weekday++
}

const total = weekend + weekday
const observedRate = total > 0 ? weekend / total : 0
const expectedRate = 3 / 7
const overrep = observedRate / expectedRate

const expected = [total * expectedRate, total * (1 - expectedRate)]
const observed = [weekend, weekday]
const chi2 = chiSquared(observed, expected)

return {
  supported: overrep > 1.0,
  effectSize: +overrep.toFixed(3),
  chiSquared: +chi2.toFixed(2),
  degreesOfFreedom: 1,
  samples: {
    total,
    weekend,
    weekday,
    weekendPercent: +(observedRate * 100).toFixed(1),
    expectedPercent: +(expectedRate * 100).toFixed(1)
  },
  summary: `${(observedRate * 100).toFixed(1)}% of sightings on Fri–Sun vs expected ${(expectedRate * 100).toFixed(1)}%. Overrepresentation: ${overrep.toFixed(3)}x. χ²(1) = ${chi2.toFixed(1)}.`
}

results.name: UAP sightings peak in Northern Hemisphere summer months
results.description: Test whether June–August accounts for more than 25% (3/12) of sightings. This tests observer availability bias (longer days, outdoor activity, July 4th).
results.summary: 30.6% of sightings in Jun–Aug vs expected 25.0%. Overrepresentation: 1.22x. Peak month: Jul (22496 sightings).

results.name: Sightings with more reported characteristics have higher credibility scores
results.description: Test whether there is a positive correlation between the number of characteristics reported and the credibility score assigned.
results.summary: Pearson r = 0.5406 across 199276 sightings. Weak positive correlation between characteristic count and credibility.
